title: Six Smartlead Alternatives for Email and LinkedIn in One Sequence
summary: Compare six Smartlead alternatives for cold email and LinkedIn in one sequence, including who each fits, LinkedIn support, unified inbox and pricing.
body_markdown:
Smartlead is built for scale: lots of inboxes, lots of clients, lots of campaigns running side by side. If you're a founder or a three-person sales team, you may be carrying complexity you never use, and still running LinkedIn in a separate tool.


This post compares six alternatives with that smaller team in mind. Some will fit you better than Smartlead, and some won't. We'll say which is which.


## Agency tool vs founder-led outbound


Smartlead earned its reputation with agencies and high-volume senders. Connecting large numbers of mailboxes, rotating sends across them, managing client sub-accounts, and white-labeling the dashboard all make sense when you run outbound for ten companies at once.


A founder-led team has a different shape. You have one offer, a handful of inboxes, and maybe one or two LinkedIn profiles. The person writing the sequence is usually the person answering the replies.


That changes what matters:


What an agency optimizes for What a small team optimizes for


Many clients, kept separate One pipeline, kept simple


Huge inbox pools and rotation A few inboxes that stay healthy


Reporting per client Knowing who replied and what to say next


Email volume first Email plus LinkedIn touches on the same person


A dedicated ops person to run it Setup in an afternoon, no onboarding call


If the left column describes you, Smartlead may already be the right tool. Stay. If the right column describes you, keep reading.


(Coming from Instantly instead? The tools overlap, but the reasons for switching differ. We cover that in[Instantly alternatives](https://supersend.io/blog/instantly-alternatives) .)


## The comparison table


How to read it: **Yes** means native at the time of writing. **Partial** means available with limits, as an add-on, or through an integration. **Check** means it changes often or we couldn't confirm it cleanly, so verify with the vendor before you decide.

Smartlead (for reference) Yes Partial / Check Yes (email) Volume tiers, check current pricing


SuperSend Yes Yes (1 to 5 senders included) Yes (email + LinkedIn) Flat monthly by email volume, unlimited contacts


Instantly Yes Check Yes (email) Tiered plans, check current pricing


lemlist Yes Yes Yes Per-user plans, check current pricing

Saleshandy Yes Check Yes (email) Tiered plans, check current pricing


We left prices out on purpose. They change too often to be useful in a blog post. What matters more is the model: are you paying per seat, per contact, per email, or per channel? That decides how your bill grows. If you do want published prices side by side, our comparison of the[best cold email software for founders](https://supersend.io/blog/best-cold-email-software) lists each plan and its cost per 1,000 emails.


## The six alternatives


### 1. SuperSend


**What it is:** An outbound sequencer for cold email and LinkedIn, built for any team that needs both channels in one sequence. Email steps and LinkedIn steps (profile visits, post likes, connection requests, wait-until-connected, messages) sit in one sequence, and a reply on either channel stops both.


**Best for:** Teams that want both channels on the same contact without stitching two tools together, and one inbox for every reply.


**Worth knowing:** It's self-serve with no demo: set up for free with no card, then a 7-day free trial starts when you launch a campaign or turn on warmup. LinkedIn senders are included (1 on Starter, 2 on Growth, 5 on Scale), and extra LinkedIn accounts are $29/month each. Plans are priced on emails sent, with unlimited contacts, and warmup is included on every inbox.


### 2. Instantly


**What it is:** An email-first cold outreach platform, known for connecting many sending accounts, built-in warmup, and a lead database.


**Best for:** Teams whose outbound is mostly email and who want a large inbox pool plus a built-in lead source in one place.


**Worth knowing:** LinkedIn has not historically been its core focus. If LinkedIn steps matter to you, check what is native today versus what needs another tool. Some products (sending, leads, CRM features) may be priced separately, so model the full stack.


### 3. lemlist


**What it is:** A multichannel outreach tool with native LinkedIn steps alongside email, plus a strong focus on personalization like custom images and landing pages.


**Best for:** Teams that want email and LinkedIn in one sequence and care a lot about creative, highly personalized touches.


**Worth knowing:** It's a mature product with a lot of surface area. Multichannel features may sit on specific plans, and per-user pricing grows with headcount, so price it against your actual team size.


### 4. Reply.io


**What it is:** A sales engagement platform covering email, LinkedIn, calls, and other channels, with AI assistance layered on top.


**Best for:** Teams that want a broader sales engagement suite with calls and manual tasks, closer to classic SDR tooling.


**Worth knowing:** More scope means more setup. Some LinkedIn actions may run automatically while others show up as manual tasks, so check which ones you need and how they behave.


### 5. Woodpecker


**What it is:** A long-running, email-focused cold outreach tool with a reputation for careful sending defaults and an agency option.


**Best for:** Email-only teams and small agencies that want a straightforward, conservative tool.


**Worth knowing:** If LinkedIn in the same sequence is a requirement, confirm current support before you migrate.


### 6. Saleshandy


**What it is:** A cold email platform that supports connecting multiple sender accounts, with a unified inbox for email replies and a lead finder.


**Best for:** Cost-conscious, email-first teams spreading volume across several inboxes.


**Worth knowing:** Check how LinkedIn is handled today, and whether the plan you want caps contacts, emails, or both.


## How to choose


Run through these in order. Most teams have their answer by question three.


1. **Count your channels.** If 90% of your outreach is email and LinkedIn is occasional, an email-first tool (Instantly, Woodpecker, Saleshandy) is fine. If you want LinkedIn touches in most sequences, shortlist tools with native LinkedIn steps: lemlist, Reply.io, or SuperSend.
2. **Count who answers replies.** If it's one or two people, a single inbox for email and LinkedIn replies saves real time. Check whether "unified inbox" in each tool includes LinkedIn or only email.
3. **Model your bill at 12 months.** Write down contacts, emails per month, seats, LinkedIn accounts, and add-ons. A per-seat tool and a per-email tool can look the same today and very different after you hire two SDRs or triple your list.
4. **Build one real sequence.** Put your actual offer into each finalist. A simple test shape: day 1 profile visit, day 2 email, day 4 connection request, day 7 follow-up email, day 9 LinkedIn message if connected. If the builder fights you on this, it will fight you every week. Our guide to[running cold email and LinkedIn in one sequence](https://supersend.io/blog/cold-email-and-linkedin-sequence) has fuller templates.
5. **Be honest about LinkedIn risk.** LinkedIn doesn't publish exact limits, and its terms restrict automation. Any tool that automates LinkedIn carries that risk, so pace conservatively. See[LinkedIn automation limits](https://supersend.io/blog/linkedin-automation-limits) for commonly cited ranges.
6. **Plan the move.** Export contacts, your unsubscribe and do-not-contact lists, and reply history before you cancel. Keep your existing domains and inboxes; most tools let you connect them, so you don't restart warmup from zero.


One more thing: don't switch mid-campaign. Let active sequences finish, then start fresh contacts in the new tool.


## The short version


- Smartlead is a strong fit for agencies and high-inbox-count senders. If that's you, switching may not help.
- Founder-led teams usually care more about email and LinkedIn in one sequence, one reply inbox, and predictable pricing.
- Several tools here, including lemlist and Reply.io, have native LinkedIn steps. Instantly, Woodpecker, and Saleshandy are email-first; check their current LinkedIn support.
- Compare pricing models, not prices: seats, contacts, emails, and add-ons all scale differently.
- Test with one real sequence before you migrate anything.


If you want email and LinkedIn in one sequence with every reply in one place, see how SuperSend is priced on the[pricing page](https://supersend.io/pricing) .
